note: Check of the DjVu baseline on the two manuals where glyph coding wins most (2026-11-28). The benchmark baseline runs cjb2 on bands of 32,760 rows (about 14 pages; DjVu's maximum page height), so one symbol dictionary is shared within each band. Splitting at real page boundaries (one dictionary per page) is worse. All decodes matched every pixel.
limits: A JBIG2 encoder with one symbol dictionary for the whole document (jbig2enc -s, minidjvu) was not available on the test machine; it could narrow the gap.
